title: Third-Party Code Signing & Build Provenance Exhibit (draft)
content:
Purpose: A contract exhibit template to attach to Master Services Agreements or Supply Agreements that codifies vendor obligations for code signing, build provenance, and artifact verification/evidence. Intended for Dedicated and Private deployments where customers require stronger supply-chain guarantees.

Status: working draft — for legal and eng-security review. Contains clause bank + minimum evidentiary checklist + operational implementation notes.

Key concepts (short):
- Code signing: vendor must sign all production artifacts with an auditable key managed according to spec below.
- Build provenance: vendor shall produce a machine-readable build provenance bundle (SBOM + build metadata + cryptographic attestations).
- Reproducible builds: where practicable, provide steps and inputs to reproduce artifacts.
- Evidence: periodic evidence delivery and on-demand audit access.

Exhibit: Third-Party Build & Signing Controls
1. Definitions (short):
  - "Artifact": any binary, container image, model weight file, package, or infrastructure-as-code template delivered to Customer.
  - "Signing Key": private key used to create a digital signature over an Artifact.
  - "Provenance Bundle": SBOM + build recipe (git refs, build env hash, toolchain versions) + signature(s) + timestamp.

2. Minimum Security Requirements
  a. Signing keys & KMS: Signing Keys used for production releases must be stored in FIPS-140-2 or equivalent certified HSM/KMS with strong access controls and multi-person authorization for key export. No Signing Key material shall be stored on developer laptops.
  b. Key Rotation: Keys used for signing must be rotated at least annually or after any suspected compromise; Customer shall be notified within 48 hours of rotation that affects delivered Artifacts.
  c. Non-repudiation: Signatures must include algorithm, key identifier, and RFC-compliant timestamping. Timestamp authority must be auditable and retention-preserved for minimum 3 years (or term of contract if longer).

3. Build Provenance & SBOM
  a. SBOM Format: Provide SPDX v2.2 (recommended) or CycloneDX, delivered as part of Provenance Bundle for every release. SBOM must list direct and transitive dependencies with source provider references and version hashes where available.
  b. Build Metadata: Include git commit hash (or equivalent immutable source ref), container image digests, build tool versions, base image digests, CI pipeline job IDs, and reproducible-build parameters.
  c. Attestation: The Provenance Bundle must be cryptographically signed by the Signing Key and reference the Artifact digest.

4. Reproducibility & Determinism
  - Vendor will document build steps and environment variables sufficient for a qualified third party to attempt a reproducible build to the extent feasible. If full bit-for-bit reproducibility is impossible (e.g., non-deterministic model training output), vendor must describe sources of non-determinism and controls to mitigate (seed management, deterministic toolchain versions, locked dependencies).

5. CI/CD Controls & Environment Hardening
  - CI pipelines used to produce production Artifacts must be protected by least-privilege credentials, ephemeral runners (where applicable), and role-based access control. Masters of pipelines must require MFA and break-glass approvals for release gates.

6. Third-Party Components and Dependency Management
  - Vendors must maintain a dependency-tracking process and a vulnerability triage workflow. Critical CVEs in direct dependencies used in production Artifacts must be patched or mitigated within 14 calendar days and Customer notified of the mitigation plan within 72 hours of discovery.

7. Audit Rights & Evidence Delivery
  a. Periodic Evidence: On a quarterly cadence, Vendor shall deliver a redacted Provenance Bundle for the latest production release and an evidence summary: key IDs, timestamp authority logs, SBOM, and CI artifact logs.
  b. On-Demand Audit: Customer may request an on-site or remote compliance review with at least 10 business days' notice. Vendor shall provide access to signing key usage logs (redacted as required), CI job records, and any SOC/ISO audit reports relevant to the controls, subject to NDAs.
  c. Emergency Access: If Customer reasonably suspects a supply-chain compromise, Vendor will provide expedited access to evidence within 48 hours and assist with mitigation.

8. Incident Response & Notification
  - If signing key compromise or confirmed tampering with provenance is detected, Vendor shall:
    * Immediately cease using affected key(s) for signing;
    * Notify Customer within 24 hours of detection;
    * Revoke the key and re-sign affected Artifacts using new keys or provide mitigations and attestations;
    * Provide a root cause analysis, impacted Artifact list, and remediation plan within 10 business days.

9. Subprocessor/Subcontractor Controls
  - Vendor must flow down these minimum requirements to any third party performing builds, artifact storage, or signing on Vendor's behalf. Vendor remains responsible for compliance and shall provide evidence of contractual flow-down upon request.

10. Liability & Remedy (clause options for negotiation)
  - Option A (lighter): Corrective remedy: priority remediation and no additional liability beyond existing indemnities.
  - Option B (stricter): Material breach for signing key compromise resulting from Vendor negligence with capped liability up to specified amount. (Legal to pick appropriate cap or carve-outs.)

11. Implementation Notes for Engineering (non-binding guidance)
  - Prefer hardware-backed keys (KMS-backed HSM). Use Sigstore/cosign for signature flow where possible. Publish transparency logs for signature entries.
  - Maintain build caches separately from developer workstations. Artifacts should be stored in immutable registries with retention and access logs.

12. Evidence Checklist (minimum items Customer will accept)
  - Signed Provenance Bundle (signed by Signing Key)
  - SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM for release
  - Artifact digest(s) (SHA256) and container image digests
  - CI/CD job IDs, build timestamps, and limited CI logs showing successful release jobs
  - KMS/HSM key metadata: key ID, creation date, rotation history, and current status (active/revoked)
  - Timestamp authority logs for signature timestamps

Open items / draft notes to counsel and sec-eng:
- Decide whether to require attestation to a specific SLSA level (3 vs 4) or leave as "reasonable commercial effort".
- Define notification SLAs for rotating keys that affect immutable delivered artifacts.
- Consider including a short-form customer verification script (bash/cosign) as an attachment showing how to verify signatures and provenance locally.

Example verification snippet (for engineering appendix):
- cosign verify-blob --key <vendor-pubkey.pem> --signature <artifact>.sig <artifact>
- Verify SBOM digest and cross-check artifact digest

Revision history: 2024-11-02 initial draft by Ava Chen; 2024-11-12 sec-eng comments added (Rafiq); 2024-11-15 legal review updates (Maya).

End of document.

Notes to self: keep this exhibit modular so we can attach to Hosted vs Private templates with light edits (e.g., stronger flow-down for Private/on-prem). Will link to sample cosign scripts and Confluence build playbook after review.
